title: Millisecond-timescale motions contribute to the function of the bacterial response regulator protein Spo0F.
experiment: 15N R1, R2 and steady-state 1H-15N heteronuclear NOE at 600 MHz (extended Lipari-Szabo Modelfree v3.1 analysis)
buffer: 1.4 mM 15N-Spo0F, 10 mM potassium phosphate, 50 mM KCl, 0.02% NaN3, 10% D2O
construct_or_mutation: wild-type full-length Bacillus subtilis apo-Spo0F (residues 1-124, uniformly 15N-labelled)
other_conditions: 仅图示 (per-residue R1, R2, NOE, S2, te and Rex profiles for 108 of 124 residues plotted in Figs. 1-2; numerical tables in unavailable Nature SI / Indiana Dynamics Database); tumbling: tm = 7:72 6 0:3 ns (7.72 ± 0.3 ns), asymmetric rotational diffusion ratio Dk/D' = 1:07 6 0:02 (isotropic; maximum artefactual Rex contribution 1.04 s-1); 10%-trimmed means: R1 = 1:49 6 0:02 s 2 1, R2 = 10:6 6 0:5 s 2 1, NOE = 0:79 6 0:01, R2/R1 = 6:86 6 0:05 ns, secondary-structure S2 = 0:89 6 0:01; Rex subset: D10-Y13, D11-G14, I15, R16-G27 (including I17, L18, L19), M55, K56, D61, M81, T82, G85, K94, T100, H101, F102, K104, F106, N124; te > 100 ps subset: I57, M60, D61 (plus extreme N- and C-termini); non-fitting residues (final models 5, 3, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4): E4, I17, I76, H101, K104, F106, N124; models 1, 1, 4: G59, K70, G85; excluded due to spectral overlap: A39, I42, K67, M89, A114, K116, L118; unobservable: 3 N-terminal residues, S123, 4 prolines
timescale: Rex > 1 s-1; Rex = 5±30 s-1 (D10-Y13 in b1-a1 loop); te > 20 ps; te > 100 ps (I57, M60, D61 and extreme termini) (extended Lipari-Szabo Modelfree v3.1 per-residue fit across 108 amides: 29 model 1, 19 model 2, 32 model 3, 5 model 4, 7 model 5)
author_claim: Regions of apo-Spo0F exhibiting microsecond-to-millisecond conformational exchange (Rex > 1 s-1, up to 5-30 s-1 in D10-Y13, clustering in the b1-a1 loop/a1-helix, ends of the b3-a3 loop, b4-a4 loop/N-terminus of a4-helix, and b5-strand/b5-a5 loop) and fast ps-ns internal motion (te > 100 ps at I57, M60, D61 in the b3-a3 loop) form a semicontiguous surface around the D54 phosphorylation site that correlates directly with residues critical for KinA, RapB, and Spo0B interactions.

caveat_note: PDF font encoding in paper.txt renders math decimals/plus-minus as colons/'6' (e.g. 'pH 6:80 6 0:05' = pH 6.80 ± 0.05) and en-dashes as '±' ('5±30 s-1' = 5-30 s-1, matching Fig. 2c y-axis 0-30 s-1). Manifest card has no BMRB ID/pH/buffer and lists sheet_temperature_K = 298.5 at 600 MHz, whereas Methods reports 300 K at 600 MHz (data deposited in Indiana Dynamics Database). Paper notes loop NOEs here differ from earlier 500 MHz study (ref. 10) due to saturation transfer errors in ref. 10; rotational anisotropy, aggregation (DLS), deamidation/oxidation (MS), and thermal denaturation (CD) were ruled out.
